paper.title: A semi-supervised learning approach to predict synthetic genetic interactions by combining functional and topological properties of functional gene network
paper.citation: You ZH, Yin Z, Han K, Huang DS, Zhou X. A semi-supervised learning approach to predict synthetic genetic interactions by combining functional and topological properties of functional gene network. BMC Bioinformatics 11:343 (2010)

inputs.name: Additional file 1 (1471-2105-11-343-S1.DOC, read, not used by the pipeline)

cause.summary: A diagram of the workflow; nothing is computed.

items.label: Abstract and Results: sensitivity 92% at specificity 91% (TPR 0.92 at FPR 0.09)

assumptions.what: Protein interactions: BioGRID two-hybrid and Affinity Capture-Western interactions of S. cerevisiae as SGD imported them on 2009-12-19 (13,007 interactions, 3,915 proteins; the paper has 12,990 and 4,478). Chosen as the interpretable filter closest to the paper's interaction count in a search over experiment-type subsets; it matches that one count only. The release's genetic interactions cover 4470 genes, close to the paper's 4,478.
assumptions.sensitivity: Every physical interaction instead: SSL 0.6531, SVM 0.6893 against 0.66 and 0.6955 (Fig. 3 setting, repeat 0).

assumptions.what: Eq. 2's W used as the tie strength (the paper calls it a confidence score) and inverted for shortest paths; the published Fig. 6 and Fig. S18 axes (weighted degrees in the hundreds, closeness above 1) fit this reading.
assumptions.sensitivity: 1 / W instead: SSL 0.6373, SVM 0.6949 (Fig. 3 setting, repeat 0; baseline SSL 0.66, SVM 0.6955).

assumptions.what: Features: sign(x) log(1 + |x|), then z-scored (the paper does not say how features were scaled).
assumptions.sensitivity: Without the log: SSL 0.6445, SVM 0.7018 (Fig. 3 setting, repeat 0; baseline SSL 0.66, SVM 0.6955).

assumptions.what: SSL: alpha = 0.99 (Zhou et al.'s value); sigma chosen among 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5 and 1 times the median distance by hiding a third of the training labels.
assumptions.sensitivity: sigma = the median distance: SSL 0.6163; alpha = 0.5: 0.6779 (Fig. 3 setting, repeat 0; baseline SSL 0.66, SVM 0.6955).

assumptions.what: SVM: scikit-learn 1.6.1 SVC (LIBSVM), RBF kernel, C in 2^-1..2^9 and gamma in 2^-9..2^1 (steps of 4x), 3-fold grid search on the training folds by area under the ROC curve.

The 18 features: the average and the absolute difference of 8 node properties (weighted degree, Barrat clustering, betweenness, closeness, eigenvector centrality; binary stress, information and current-flow betweenness), the weighted shortest path, and the number of mutual neighbours.

Non-SGI pairs: Tong 2004 query genes x the deletion array (Verified and Uncharacterized ORFs without an inviable systematic deletion, 4,747 genes) with no reported Tong 2004 interaction, both genes in the network.
assumptions.sensitivity: Random gene pairs instead: SSL 0.7249, SVM 0.7666 (Fig. 3 setting, repeat 0; baseline SSL 0.66, SVM 0.6955).

assumptions.what: Five repeats with seeds 0-4; test scores ranked within each fold and pooled; repeats averaged at 26 score quantiles (threshold averaging), which also place the drawn markers.

Expression: SGD's processed copies of Cho 1998 (17 conditions), Chu 1998 sporulation (7), Spellman 1998 alpha factor (16) and elutriation (14): 54 conditions, not 64. Eisen 1998's 6 heat-shock points were not reachable.

cause.summary: Not reproduced with the network the Methods describe (protein interactions and complexes): areas under the ROC curve 0.675 to 0.645 for SSL and 0.705 to 0.678 for SVM; the published curves enclose 0.963, 0.912 and 0.875 (SSL) and 0.878, 0.818 and 0.74 (SVM), read from Figs 2-4. The published level comes back once BioGRID's genetic interactions are in the network (Fig. 3 setting: SSL 0.859, SVM 0.9096 without Tong 2004's own rows, 0.89 and 0.9587 with them); these edges carry the SGI labels into the features. Open: the authors' exact network, and the order of the two classifiers (SVM stays ahead of SSL in every variant we ran).

hypotheses.hypothesis: Our classifier settings are off: the SSL length scale or alpha.
hypotheses.test: Fig. 3 setting, repeat 0: SSL with sigma = the median distance (no selection), and with alpha = 0.5 instead of 0.99. SSL area under the ROC curve 0.6163 and 0.6779 against 0.66; the published curves enclose 0.963, 0.912 and 0.875 (SSL) and 0.878, 0.818 and 0.74 (SVM) at 20, 50 and 80% unlabelled, read from Figs 2-4.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Our protein-interaction filter is wrong (the paper gives only 'BioGrid').
hypotheses.test: Every physical interaction except Gavin's and Ho's (44,346 edges) in place of two-hybrid plus Affinity Capture-Western. SSL 0.6531, SVM 0.6893 (ours 0.66, 0.6955).

hypotheses.hypothesis: Eq. 2's W is a distance, so the tie strength is 1 / W.
hypotheses.test: Weighted network rebuilt with 1 / W. SSL 0.6373, SVM 0.6949.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Our feature scaling hides the signal.
hypotheses.test: Features z-scored without the log transform. SSL 0.6445, SVM 0.7018.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The non-SGI pairs were random gene pairs, not tested pairs.
hypotheses.test: 1,500 random pairs of network genes (no reported SGI) as negatives. SSL 0.7249, SVM 0.7666 (Fig. 3 setting, repeat 0; baseline SSL 0.66, SVM 0.6955): higher, but far from the published curves.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Our network measures are computed wrongly.
hypotheses.test: Stress, current-flow betweenness and information centrality checked against networkx and a brute-force path count on random graphs (package tests).

hypotheses.hypothesis: The paper's pair-level cross-validation lets a gene's identity carry from training to test pairs: each Tong query gene sits in many pairs.
hypotheses.test: SVM and SSL on one-hot gene identity alone, no network: SSL 0.8124, SVM 0.8874 (Fig. 3 setting, repeat 0; baseline SSL 0.66, SVM 0.6955). Every test pair shares a gene with the training pairs (1.0 of them), 0.5473 share both. A problem with the paper's evaluation: its AUCs measure, in part, which genes are SGI hubs.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The authors' 'BioGrid' network included genetic interactions. Many Tong SGI pairs are reported again by other papers (1899 of 3411), so the labels become edges of the network.
hypotheses.test: Our network plus the genetic interactions of papers other than Tong 2004 (107926 edges; 882 of the 1,500 sampled SGI pairs and 18 non-SGI pairs become edges): SSL 0.859, SVM 0.9096 (Fig. 3 setting, repeat 0; baseline SSL 0.66, SVM 0.6955); the published Fig. 3 curves enclose 0.912 (SSL) and 0.818 (SVM). With every genetic interaction, Tong 2004 included: SSL 0.89, SVM 0.9587. Suggested by a reviewer (hyunhwan-bcm) on the pull request.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Genetic interactions help beyond the leaked labels (genes with many genetic partners are SGI hubs).
hypotheses.test: The same network with every Tong SGI pair removed from the added edges: SSL 0.8328, SVM 0.8674.
